topicName: Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Information Extraction
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Information Extraction in NLP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a fundamental subtask of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that focuses on locating and classifying named entities mentioned in unstructured text into pre-defined categories such as person names, organizations, locations, medical codes, time expressions, quantities, and monetary values."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Information Extraction Pipeline"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Information Extraction (IE) is the broader process of turning unstructured text into structured, machine-readable data. The typical IE pipeline consists of several sequential stages:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tokenization: Breaking down the raw text into individual words or sub-words."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Part-of-Speech (POS) Tagging: Identifying the grammatical role of each token."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Named Entity Recognition (NER): Classifying specific nouns into predefined entity classes."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Relation Extraction: Determining semantic relationships between identified entities."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing NER with Python and spaCy"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The spaCy library provides a robust, production-ready implementation of Named Entity Recognition. Below is a practical example demonstrating how to load a pre-trained pipeline and extract entities from text."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"import spacy

# Load the small English transformer/pipeline
nlp = spacy.load('en_core_web_sm')

text = 'Apple Inc. plans to open a new retail store in San Francisco by next month, according to CEO Tim Cook.'
doc = nlp(text)

for ent in doc.ents:
    print(f'Entity: {ent.text} | Label: {ent.label_}')"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Common NER Evaluation Metrics"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To evaluate the performance of an NER model, we primarily rely on entity-level Precision, Recall, and the F1-Score rather than token-level accuracy. An entity prediction is considered completely correct only if both its boundary (start and end tokens) and its semantic class label match the gold standard."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Precision: The ratio of correctly predicted entities to the total entities predicted by the model."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Recall: The ratio of correctly predicted entities to the total actual entities in the ground truth."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"F1-Score: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a single metric for model evaluation."}]
